outcome: increased sulcus angle (SA) of the femoral trochlea
cohort: The study included 85 newborns (170 knees), comprising healthy infants born in breech presentation (31-42 weeks gestation) and those born in cephalic presentation (35-41 weeks gestation).
finding: Newborns with breech presentation exhibit significantly higher sulcus angle values compared to those born in cephalic presentation, suggesting a flatter trochlear groove and a potential predisposition to patellofemoral joint instability.
mod_finding: The rate of caesarean-section deliveries was significantly higher in the breech presentation group compared to the cephalic presentation group.
birth_weight: Breech presentation group: 3091.71 g (SD=500.94); Cephalic presentation group: 3380.74 g (SD=424.72).
gest_age: Breech presentation group: 31-42 weeks (mean 267 days); Cephalic presentation group: 35-41 weeks (mean 274 days).
